W.notes: Strengths: a compact, readable server.mjs (325 lines). serialize() at server.mjs:129-134 orders creates and deletes; the rule checks run before the queue and the overlap check inside it (server.mjs:142-182). save() (server.mjs:136-140) updates memory only after writeFile succeeds. readBody (server.mjs:93-118) counts every byte while keeping at most 10001. Ran: npm test gave 20/20 passing. My probe passed 102/102 (concurrency, save failure, restart, routing, all rules). Defects: parseStore (server.mjs:49-65) does not check the top-level keys, so a data file {"nextId":1,"bookings":[],"junk":1} is accepted and the server starts listening, though it is not the layout this server writes (X, Y and Z exit 1). It also allows overlapping stored bookings. Tests are thin: 20 coarse tests bundle many assertions, with few edge cases on the page side (app.test.mjs is 5 tests). README is only 44 lines and short on error and exit details. The app.js `.apply` spread is old-style.

X.notes: Strengths: after the body is read, request handling is fully synchronous, including fs.writeFileSync at server.mjs:96-98. That makes requests effectively one at a time with no queue, and createStore.commit (server.mjs:258-267) saves before swapping state. Routes are a table at server.mjs:124-129 with a small route() at server.mjs:108-122. The data-file check (server.mjs:62-76) rejects extra keys, duplicate ids and overlaps. main (server.mjs:278-304) sets exitCode instead of calling exit abruptly, and gives a fixed PORT message to keep stderr to one line. Ran: npm test gave 132/132 passing (server, page, final). My probe passed 102/102. README is about 180 lines. Weaknesses: the synchronous write blocks the event loop during saves; readBody (server.mjs:218-227) never settles if the client aborts mid-body (no close handler, so the request is silently dropped); sendStatic re-reads the files on every request.

Y.notes: Strengths: server.mjs:137-146 saves atomically (write a temp file, rename it over, clean up on error), and commit (server.mjs:243-247) changes memory only after the save. server.mjs:318-335 sends every request through one global queue, so concurrency is trivially correct. server.mjs:360-363 has a clientError handler; server.mjs:301-305 logs unexpected errors to stderr on one line; server.mjs:106-116 checks the data file strictly. MSG constants are at server.mjs:25-39. Ran: npm test gave 288/288 passing across 7 well-named files (static page, page behaviour, booking rules, routes, persistence, startup). My probe passed 102/102. README is about 210 lines and thorough. Weaknesses: the temp file `<file>.<pid>.tmp` is an extra write next to the data file, and rename replaces symlinks; the global queue also serialises GETs and static files behind slow saves.

Z.notes: Strengths: server.mjs:206-226 holds the store in a repository whose commit saves first and only then swaps the state (frozen), and which runs creates and deletes one at a time, so a failed save keeps the next id. server.mjs:95-107 checks the data file strictly (exact keys, ids below nextId, unique ids, no overlaps); line 103 also requires nextId+1 to stay a safe integer, so a saved file always reloads. server.mjs:309-331 routes cleanly, with the /api/bookings/ prefix handled before the static files. server.mjs:357-358 lets the stderr write finish before exiting. app.js:33-52 has one request() returning ok, error or none, matching the spec's reply model. Ran: npm test gave 607/607 passing (fake-DOM page tests, startup, persistence, body and field rules). My probe passed 102/102, and it rejected the data file with an extra key. README is about 205 lines, detailed. Minor: fieldError (server.mjs:70-78) uses ROOMS.includes without a typeof check (harmless); there is no clientError handler; about 400 lines with some ceremony (Object.freeze everywhere).

W.notes: Own tests: 20/20 pass; broad but shallow (few rule edge cases). Data-file check too loose, server.mjs:49-65: a file with an extra top-level key ({"nextId":1,"bookings":[],"x":1}) or with overlapping bookings started normally instead of printing 'cannot read data file' and exiting 1 (confirmed by probe). server.mjs:285 echoes the raw PORT value, so a PORT containing a newline breaks the one-line rule. Otherwise passed the API/routing/concurrency/persistence/failed-save probes; serialized commit in server.mjs:128-140. README (44 lines) is brief but usable.

X.notes: Own tests: 132/132 pass (server, page app with overlapping list fetches, final checks). Passed every black-box probe. server.mjs:96-98 synchronous writeFileSync makes concurrency trivially correct but blocks the event loop during saves; route table at server.mjs:108-129 is tidy; exits cleanly via process.exitCode (server.mjs:283). server.mjs:226 body reader ignores aborted requests without settling them (harmless in probes). Fixed PORT error text avoids multi-line stderr. Good README with examples.

Y.notes: Own tests: 288/288 pass (routes, rules, persistence, startup, static page checks, fake-DOM page behaviour). Passed every black-box probe, same set as W. server.mjs:137-146 saves via temp file + rename, so a failed save never corrupts the old file; server.mjs:318-335 handles all requests one at a time (simple and correct, but slow saves hold up reads); server.mjs:360 handles clientError; HttpError makes the flow clean. Strict data-file check (server.mjs:106-116). Thorough README with status codes and data format. Slightly behind W on test depth.

Z.notes: Own tests: 607/607 pass, including fake-DOM page tests (stale list fetches, cancel/submit), concurrency and persistence. Passed every black-box probe: startup errors (bad PORT, PORT checked before the data file, empty / extra-key / overlapping / directory data file, port in use), rules 1-10 in order, BOM, invalid UTF-8, chunked 413, 415/413 on a 300KB body, byte-exact routing via raw sockets, 30 concurrent overlapping POSTs -> exactly 1 x 201 and 29 x 409, unique ids, restart keeps bookings and next id, failed save -> 500 with nothing changed and no folder created. server.mjs:206-226 queue that commits only after a successful save; server.mjs:95-107 strict data-file check (even keeps nextId+1 safe). Minor: server.mjs:349 logs 'server error: ECONNRESET' on every aborted client. README covers env vars, startup, API and data file in detail.

W.notes: Ran npm test: 142/142 pass. Probe (startup, concurrency, 413/415, routing, persistence, save failure): all pass. Strengths: one validator for both POST bodies and the data file, which is checked strictly (key set, ids below nextId, no overlaps) at server.mjs:58-84; mutations run one at a time and the store changes only after the write succeeds (server.mjs:180-193); a single HttpError path maps errors to replies (server.mjs:267-278). public/app.js:47-70 re-enables the button through an onSettle callback the moment the request settles, which matches the spec closely; stale list replies are dropped by a counter (app.js:135-141). Defects: a request with `Expect: foo` gets Node's 417 and a CONNECT request is dropped with no reply (the server never handles checkExpectation or connect); on 500 it does not log the cause anywhere (server.mjs:276). README (146 lines) is thorough: env vars, startup errors, rules, examples.

X.notes: Ran npm test: 306/306 pass across 7 test files plus a fake DOM. Probe: all pass. Strengths: error messages kept in one MSG table (server.mjs:22-36); rules 1-3 and 4-9 split into pure functions (server.mjs:73-83, 189-199); mutations serialized (server.mjs:208-218); the cause of a 500 goes to stderr, never stdout (server.mjs:301); the most complete README (218 lines, every route and the exit codes). The fail() helper exits only after the stderr write has flushed (server.mjs:100-102). Defects: same as W for `Expect: foo` (417) and CONNECT (dropped); validateFields destructures with inherited lookups (server.mjs:74), harmless for JSON.parse output; the client fills rooms with append rather than replaceChildren (public/app.js:124), fine on the first load.

Y.notes: Ran npm test: 489/489 pass across 10 test files with HTML-tree and fake-DOM helpers. Probe: all pass, and it was the only one that answered `Expect: foo` with a normal 200 (server.mjs:365) and CONNECT on a known path with 405 (server.mjs:267-276, 366). Strengths: an aborted request body is rejected rather than processed (server.mjs:153-155); every request goes through one queue (server.mjs:300-308, 333) so all orderings are consistent; a store abstraction with commit-after-write (server.mjs:310-319); a separate bind-error handler is swapped for a logging one after listen (server.mjs:367-371). Client app.js mirrors the spec closely. Defects: sortBookings builds key arrays on every comparison (server.mjs:167-175), more convoluted than needed; GETs wait behind slow writes in the shared queue; README (112 lines) is shorter than W's or X's but covers usage, env vars, data file, API and rules.

Z.notes: Ran npm test: 20/20 pass; there are few, broad tests (startup, routing, rules, concurrency, persistence, save failure, plus a small DOM test). Probe: all core checks pass (concurrency 1x201/9x409, unique ids, 413/415, BOM, routing, restart, 500 on save failure with no folder created). Defects: the whole server is top-level script state (server.mjs:112-134, 141), less modular and harder to test; readBody resolves on 'close' (server.mjs:189), so a body cut off by a client abort is still processed; `Expect: foo` gets 417 and CONNECT gets no reply; on a 200 list reply with a malformed body the client renders 'No bookings.' instead of an error (public/app.js:79); var-style client code. README is minimal (41 lines): usage, env vars, an API table and a curl example, with no listing of the validation rules or the error messages.

W.notes: Passed every probe and the page harness. Strengths: an HttpError class makes routing linear (server.mjs:19-24, 233-278); the body is buffered only for POST /api/bookings but always drained (server.mjs:101-112, 239-240); immutable frozen state (server.mjs:83, 201-202); the save error maps to 500 without changing state (server.mjs:186-193); app.js re-enables Book/Cancel exactly at settle via a callback (public/app.js:50-73). Weaknesses: parseStore only checks the key count, not the key names (server.mjs:77; still rejects bad files via later checks); the 409 lookup sorts to find the earliest overlap (server.mjs:197-199), fine but less direct; readBody has no abort handling (server.mjs:101-112). Tests: 142 tests in 2 large files (server.test.mjs 715 lines, app.test.mjs 616 lines) with a fake DOM; all pass. README (146 lines) is clear on env vars, startup errors, data file and API.

X.notes: Passed every probe and the page harness. Strengths: very readable, pure validators shared between requests and the data file (server.mjs:43-90, 111-129); commit-then-swap inside the serialize queue (server.mjs:208-218, 233-252); one try/catch turns any failure into 500 and logs only a code to stderr (server.mjs:294-304); fail() exits after the stderr write flushes (server.mjs:100-102). app.js is clean (public/app.js:24-37 request wrapper, 88-109 sequence guard). Weaknesses: readBody has no close/aborted handling (server.mjs:165-180); it relies on Node emitting an error on abort, which it does (ECONNRESET seen on stderr). Tests: 306 tests over 6 files plus support helpers, covering HTML structure, page booking flows and server rules; all pass. README (218 lines) is the most detailed.

Y.notes: Passed every probe and the page harness. Strengths: clean main()/store/handlers split (server.mjs:202-244, 310-319); the whole route runs inside a queue so state is read fresh, which makes concurrency trivially correct (server.mjs:321-339); aborted bodies are rejected and the socket destroyed (server.mjs:153-155); CONNECT gets a 405/404 on the raw socket (server.mjs:267-276); checkExpectation routing avoids Node's automatic 417 (server.mjs:365); a missing Content-Type is checked via typeof (server.mjs:160); data-file validation is thorough (server.mjs:88-107). Concise causes go to stderr only, never stdout. Weaknesses: every request is serialised, GETs included (minor throughput cost); the sortBookings key-array comparator is over-clever (server.mjs:167-175). Tests: 489 tests in 10 well-organised files with fake-DOM and HTML-tree helpers covering page structure, stale fetches and persistence; all pass. README (112 lines) covers env vars, data-file layout, API and errors.

Z.notes: Fully correct in all my probes (startup, ~130 API cases, 20-way concurrency, persistence/restart, save-failure rollback for POST and DELETE, fake-DOM page harness). Strengths: compact, readable server.mjs; validation reused for data-file checks (server.mjs:82-108); state committed only after save (server.mjs:226-233, 243-250); a single queue serialises mutations (server.mjs:141-146); readBody counts every byte but keeps at most 10001 and resolves on close too (server.mjs:170-196); the page script is minimal and correct, with a list sequence guard (public/app.js:73-91). Weaknesses: tests are thin, 20 tests in 2 files; W/test/server.test.mjs:168 only regex-checks the page, with no label/form/element structure tests; booking-rule tables are small (server.test.mjs:180-223). README (README.md, 41 lines) is minimal and omits the error messages and data-file layout. app.js:58 uses spread with replaceChildren (fine). npm test: 20/20 pass.

W.notes: Strengths: atomic temp-file+rename save with temp cleanup (W/server.mjs:136-146); promise-chain lock serialises mutations, and state is committed only after a successful save, so a failed save changes nothing, next id included (server.mjs:201-210); strict data-file layout validation including id<nextId, duplicate ids and overlaps (server.mjs:91-121); exact byte-for-byte routing (server.mjs:265-292); page script ignores stale list fetches with a ticket counter and treats unreadable bodies as no reply (public/app.js:35-51, 82-99). Ran: npm test 322/322 pass; my probes 18/18 startup, 74/74 API (apart from the fetch-normalisation artifact; raw socket gives 404 for /api/./rooms), 12/12 persistence (500 on missing folder, next id preserved, no tmp leftovers), 21/22 fake-DOM page checks (the one miss was a bug in my probe). Weaknesses: no handling of CONNECT (connection dropped) or requests without a Host header (Node default 400); the temp file needs create permission in the data folder (server.mjs:138). README is very complete (273 lines: env vars, exit codes, API).

X.notes: Strengths: a repository with a serialised mutate queue that commits only after writeFile succeeds (X/server.mjs:153-170); clear route table with 404 before 405 (server.mjs:263-288); goes beyond the spec by answering CONNECT on the raw socket (server.mjs:312-322), handling Expect via checkExpectation and accepting requests without a Host header (requireHostHeader:false, server.mjs:349-350), so every method gets 404/405 JSON as the task wants; the error reply itself is guarded against throwing (server.mjs:301-309); page script uses a finally-based onSettle so Book and Cancel re-enable before anything else (public/app.js:24-40). Ran: npm test 414/414 pass (the largest suite, split by concern, with a fake DOM); my probes 18/18 startup, 74/74 API (the only solution where CONNECT returns 405 and a missing Host returns 200), 12/12 persistence, 21/22 page checks (the one miss was my probe's fault). Weakness: saves use a plain writeFile, not atomic, so a crash mid-write could corrupt the data file (server.mjs:161). Good README.

Y.notes: Strengths: compact and correct; synchronous validation plus writeFileSync makes requests serialise naturally (Y/server.mjs:261-264, 302-343); strict data-file layout check (server.mjs:206-229); page script handles stale fetches and the no-reply cases correctly (script at server.mjs:128-144). Ran: npm test 10/10 pass; my probes 18/18 startup, 74/74 API (no-Host/CONNECT not handled, like W and Z), 12/12 persistence, 21/22 page checks (the one miss was my probe's fault). Weaknesses: the whole HTML page and app.js live as template strings inside server.mjs (server.mjs:8-183), which is hard to maintain and lint; only 10 coarse tests; non-atomic save (server.mjs:262); the listen error handler would exit on any later server 'error' (server.mjs:409); loadRooms throws an unhandled error if rooms is not an array (server.mjs:82). Minimal 34-line README, though accurate.

Z.notes: Strengths: fully synchronous handling once the body is read, so concurrency is trivially correct (Z/server.mjs:291-303); atomic sync temp+rename save with cleanup (server.mjs:140-154); strict layout validation, and the data file is decoded with a fatal TextDecoder keeping the BOM (server.mjs:122-138); specific listen error lines (server.mjs:156-163). Ran: npm test 216/216 pass; my probes 18/18 startup, 74/74 API, 12/12 persistence, 21/22 page checks (the one miss was my probe's fault). Weaknesses: synchronous readFileSync for the page on every request blocks the event loop (server.mjs:177-181); a successful list reply missing 'bookings' silently renders 'No bookings.' instead of an error (public/app.js:105); exceptions in .then handlers go unhandled (public/app.js:51-63); no CONNECT or no-Host handling; fewer tests than W and X. README is clear (177 lines).

W.notes: Strengths: atomic temp-file + rename save with cleanup (server.mjs:136-146); a serialized lock around the overlap check and commit (server.mjs:201-257), so a failed save leaves the state and next id unchanged; ownField avoids reading inherited properties (server.mjs:54-56); explicit comment explaining the ASCII-only case folding (server.mjs:181); data file validated, including ids below nextId and no overlaps (server.mjs:91-121). My 109-check script passed every functional check: concurrency, byte limits, BOM, invalid UTF-8, restart persistence, 500 on save failure, no folders created. Client public/app.js:35-51 cleanly separates 'reached' from 'ok' and shape-checks replies. npm test: 322/322 pass across 10 test files, including fake-DOM client tests. Very thorough 273-line README. Defects: same as W, CONNECT gets no reply, a missing Host gets Node's 400, and Expect: foo gets 417; the 'error' handler exits even on errors after listening (server.mjs:340); index.html carries a large inline style block (fine, but noise).

X.notes: Strengths: the most complete handling of the spec's edge cases: CONNECT is answered on the raw socket (server.mjs:312-322), HTTP/1.1 requests without Host are accepted (server.mjs:349), and odd Expect headers go through the normal handler (server.mjs:350). My 109-check script showed only the 3 errors in my own script (fetch normalising dot-segments, and two miscounted ids), and Y alone passed the CONNECT, no-Host and Expect: foo probes. Clean repository with a serialized mutate queue; the state is committed only after the write succeeds (server.mjs:153-170); frozen state; MSG table (server.mjs:21-35); route table with the 404/405 split (server.mjs:263-288); replyWithError guards against throwing during the reply (server.mjs:301-309). Client: the send() finally hook re-enables buttons before the outcome is used (public/app.js:24-41), and replies are shape-checked. npm test: 414/414 across 11 well-organised files (startup, request-body, routing, page-script-api, ...). Detailed 211-line README. Defects: writeFile in place, not atomic (server.mjs:161); a crash mid-write could truncate the data file.

Y.notes: Strengths: a single file with the page and script embedded as strings (server.mjs:8-183); correct validation and error order (server.mjs:302-343); the 409 picks the earliest overlap by sorting (server.mjs:333-338); data-file layout validated (server.mjs:206-229). Passed all functional checks in my 109-check script, including the concurrency check (handling after the body is read is synchronous) and 500 with nothing changed on save failure. Defects: non-atomic writeFileSync straight onto the data file (server.mjs:261-264), so a partial write could truncate it; the client's success handlers don't check the reply shape, so a malformed 200 body throws an unhandled rejection (server.mjs:82, 139); 'error' handler after listen still exits the process (server.mjs:409); CONNECT gets no reply, a missing Host gets Node's 400, Expect: foo gets 417. Tests: only 10 tests (test/server.test.mjs, test/app.test.mjs), all pass, but coarse. README is 34 lines: usage and API table, little else.

Z.notes: Strengths: compact synchronous design that makes concurrent requests serial by construction (server.mjs:2-3, 291-303); atomic save via temp file + rename with cleanup (server.mjs:140-154), so a failed save changes nothing and uses up no id; strict data-file layout check (server.mjs:78-104), with the file decoded as fatal UTF-8 (server.mjs:132); ASCII-only case folding of the media type (server.mjs:204-208); byte-exact routing (server.mjs:248-273). My 109-check script passed every functional check (startup errors, all 10 booking rules, BOM, invalid UTF-8, 10000 vs 10001 bytes, 20 concurrent overlapping POSTs giving one 201, restart persistence, 500 on save failure). Client public/app.js:33-45 treats a JSON parse failure as no reply, and the newest list fetch wins (app.js:94-110). npm test: 216/216 pass, including fake-DOM client tests. Defects: CONNECT gets no reply at all, an HTTP/1.1 request without Host gets Node's 400 instead of the API's reply, and Expect: foo gets a bare 417 (raw-socket probes); synchronous fs calls block the event loop during saves.
